title: The Euler characteristic of a perfect complex is well defined on the derived category and additive on distinguished triangles
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts the existence of a map c from perfect complexes over R to K_0(R) with three properties: sign behaviour under shifts, additivity on distinguished triangles, and agreement with the alternating sum of classes for a finite complex of finite projective modules (source lines 36490-36505). The proof defines c(K) = sum (-1)^n [M^n] and must show this is independent of the representative (proof lines 36507-36517). It does so in two stages: for a surjection of finite complexes of finite projective modules with kernel K^bullet, the degreewise short exact sequences split because each M^n is projective, giving additivity c(L) = c(K) + c(M) (proof lines 36519-36529); and for an acyclic M^bullet, the complex is broken into the displayed chain of short exact sequences and a descending induction shows each N^i is finite projective, the sequences split, and the alternating sum telescopes to zero (proof lines 36531-36549). Well-definedness and additivity on triangles then follow formally (proof lines 36551-36557). The non-routine step is the telescoping computation for acyclic complexes, which is what makes c well defined.
